He trained within a family active in real estate for three generations before establishing his own business. long_biography.plain_text:
Property developer Byron Baciocchi planned the iLife project in Etoy around the practical work of buying and fitting out a home. The complex was intended to bring showrooms, design retailers and professional services together, allowing customers to find tradespeople, architects, insurers and bankers in one location. Separate buildings were planned for retail galleries, showrooms and offices.

At Ultima, he and his partner developed income beyond accommodation by selling displayed artworks, furniture and interior-design services. Staff first worked at the Gstaad hotel before moving between properties as bookings required. The hotel also adjusted staffing seasonally while remaining open through quieter months.
